# Auto claims guidelines (excerpts)

Authority: senior desk adjusters may pay up to $15,000 per claim (indemnity) and set reserves up to $25,000.
Above that, the supervisor; above $50,000 or any policy-limits demand, the Claims Manager.
Texas first-party deadlines (Ins. Code ch. 542): acknowledge, begin the investigation and request what you
need within 15 days of notice; accept or reject in writing within 15 business days of receiving all items
(business days exclude weekends and Texas holidays, including Veterans Day 11/11 and Thanksgiving 11/26-27); if
you need more time, tell the claimant why in writing, and decide within 45 days of that notice; pay within 5
business days of accepting.
Total losses: ACV from the CCC valuation, less the deductible; send the valuation report with the offer.
Owners may dispute with comparable vehicles; review them in good faith. The appraisal clause is available.
Liability: any time-limited demand, any demand at or above limits, or any claim with specials above 50% of the
limit is reported to the supervisor and Claims Manager the same day, with a copy to the insured (excess
letter) and defense counsel if in suit. Never let a time-limited demand lapse without a decision.
Fraud indicators: refer to SIU with the facts. Don't accuse, deny or delay a claim for suspicion alone;
continue handling in parallel unless SIU says otherwise.
Payments: confirm payee and amount against the file; report any duplicate or overpayment to Claims Payments.

deductible. Other than collision losses include hail.

necessary to repair or replace it.
Transportation expenses: up to $30 per day, to a maximum of $900, beginning 24 hours after a covered loss.
Appraisal: if we and you disagree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal.

documents.title: Auto claims guidelines, part 2: contact, third parties, PIP, subrogation, titles, litigation

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Auto claims guidelines, part 2 (excerpts)

Contact: reach the insured and every claimant within one business day of assignment; three attempts logged in
ClaimCenter, then a contact letter. An acknowledgment made by phone is recorded in the case note with its date,
manner and content (Ins. Code 542.055(c)); send a written acknowledgment with the list of what you need.
Recorded statements: ask permission on the recording and note it; never record without it.
Represented claimants: once a claimant has an attorney, communicate about the claim only through the attorney.
Policy limits and insured information: do not disclose the insured's limits, statement, declarations or other
personal information to a third party or their attorney without the insured's written consent, a subpoena or a
suit. Tell the requester you will ask the insured. Never share a claimant's medical information outside the file
(agents included).
Third-party property damage: the claimant chooses the repair facility (Ins. Code 1952.301(b)); offer our
direct-repair shops only as an option. Loss of use: a rental of similar class for the reasonable repair time.
No deductible applies to a third-party claim.
Comparative fault: set liability as a percentage from the facts (crash report, statements, scene). The
claimant's damages are reduced by the claimant's percentage; above 50%, no recovery (Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code
33.001, 33.012). Explain the percentage and the reasons in writing, and offer to review new evidence.
First-party repairs: the insured chooses the shop (Ins. Code 1952.301(a)). The policy pays the cost to repair or
the actual cash value, whichever is less; it does not pay diminished value.
PIP (Ins. Code 1952.156): pay each benefit within 30 days of satisfactory proof, up to the PIP limit on the
declarations. When a payment exhausts the limit, tell the insured in writing.
Uninsured motorist property damage: a hit-and-run needs actual physical contact with the insured's vehicle
(Ins. Code 1952.104). UMPD carries a $250 deductible on our policies.
Subrogation: demand the gross loss, including the insured's deductible. The insured's deductible is refunded in
the same proportion as the recovery (recovery percentage x deductible). The Subrogation Specialist negotiates;
the handling adjuster recommends on liability. Unresolved disputes go to intercompany arbitration.
Total loss titles: get the title within 30 days of payment. If the owner does not send it, send two written
requests; the Total Loss Unit may then apply to TxDMV, no earlier than the 30th day after payment, with a
statement that two written notices were sent (Transp. Code 501.0925).
Owner-retained salvage: the settlement is the ACV less the deductible less the salvage value (the salvage bid in
the file). The owner receives a salvage title and must have the vehicle repaired and re-titled before driving it.
Litigation billing (panel counsel): partner $185 an hour, associate $150, paralegal $95, in tenths. No block
billing (an entry combining tasks over 1.0 hour is cut to 1.0). Routine correspondence: up to 0.2 hour each.
Clerical work (scheduling, copying, Bates-stamping, filing) is not billable. Travel at half rate. Computer
research charges are overhead. Approve within 30 days and explain each reduction to counsel.
Fraud: SIU makes the reports to the TDI fraud unit (Ins. Code 701.051). Adjusters refer to SIU.
Complaints: Compliance answers TDI. Send Compliance the file timeline by the date they ask for.
Payment security: change a payee's bank account or address only after calling the payee at the number already
in ClaimCenter. Forward suspicious payment-change requests to IT Security (security@) and do not reply to them.
CAT coding: every hail or wind claim from the 10/29 storm is coded CAT 2610. A collision during the storm
(wet road, low visibility) is not a catastrophe claim and is not CAT-coded.
